title: perf: improve copyZeroAlloc for os.File and net.TCPConn

source.license_note: Real upstream fasthttp optimization PR #1893; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up copyZeroAlloc so it avoids the WriterTo/ReaderFrom fallback that silently degrades to io.Copy for os.File and net.TCPConn, restoring sendfile-style zero-copy on the right type pairs without changing behavior.
task.instructions: Optimize copyZeroAlloc in http.go for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkCopyZeroAllocOSFileToStringsBuilder measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: copyZeroAlloc blindly calls WriteTo/ReadFrom; for os.File and net.TCPConn these fall back to io.Copy when sendfile is impossible, and the generic io.CopyBuffer path re-checks interfaces it already ruled out.

ops_fault.description: copyZeroAlloc in http.go uses io.WriterTo/io.ReaderFrom unconditionally; for os.File and net.TCPConn the WriterTo fallback calls io.Copy instead of sendfile, and the io.CopyBuffer fallback redundantly re-checks WriterTo/ReaderFrom.
detection_keywords: sendfile not triggered between os.File and net.TCPConn
copyZeroAlloc not zero-copy for file/conn pairs
repair_keywords: use ReadFrom only when sendfile is possible
custom copyBuffer helper without re-checking interfaces

visible_context.issue_text: copyZeroAlloc relies on the WriterTo/ReaderFrom interfaces, but os.File and net.TCPConn fall back to a plain io.Copy inside their WriterTo when sendfile is not possible, so the intended zero-copy path is silently lost on certain type pairs.
